NextDoor.Company started as a weekend hackathon project because I kept seeing growth news about startups and their hiring spree, but at the same time my friends kept complaining: "If startups are hiring actively, where are they?" or "I can't find good startups on LinkedIn or Indeed anymore."  
  
So I built a map-first job discovery platform that shows you top-tier startups actively hiring near you. Since August last year, I've been hand curating top-tier startups globally, and now it hosts 16,000+ live job openings, updated every week. [...] Framer AI Agents

results.title: How to find startup jobs in India that aren't on Naukri or LinkedIn | Sankalp Sinha posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content: learning, the real impact you can make from day one. You're not just another hire. You're building the foundation. But here's the catch: if you don't know these companies exist, you can't apply to them. That's the broken part. Job seekers are stuck applying to the same crowded roles at well-known companies. Startups are stuck trying to find talent through fragmented channels. Both sides lose. This is why I'm building NextDoor.Company. It puts startup hiring on a map so you can actually see who's hiring around you. Not just the big names. All the startups you've never heard of but should know about. Just yesterday, a user of NextDoor messaged me and I couldn't be happier reading it: "I got one internship perfect for my role and I applied for it! I don't think I'd have come across it if it [...] You and most of your friends/peers are missing out on 90% of startup jobs in India. Here's why. I spent the last month talking to job seekers in India while building NextDoor.Company. Here's what I learned: most of them are applying to the same 20-40 companies they see on Naukri or LinkedIn. The problem? Those aren't the only startups hiring. There are hundreds of early to mid stage startups in India desperately looking for talent. But they're hard to discover. Some post on job boards, some share on social media, some just rely on their network. These startups sometimes pay at par or above the market compensation (I've seen it first hand). But what they offer is something else entirely. The speed at which you grow, the depth of learning, the real impact you can make from day one. You're [...] applied for it! I don't think I'd have come across it if it wasn't for NextDoorCompany." That's exactly what I'm trying to solve. There's a hidden startup job market in India, and most people can't access it because discovery is broken. If you're job hunting right now, try this. Search for startups in your city that just raised funding. Look at their team page. See if they're hiring. You'll be surprised how many opportunities you find that weren't on your radar. The best opportunities aren't always the most visible ones.
